source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)

verses.translation: And on the first [day] of the week, at early dawn [or: at the breaking of morning], they came to the sepulchre, carrying spices and anointing oils that they had prepared

translation_notes: בת (consonants ב-ת): Candidates: H1323 'daughter', H1324 'bath (liquid measure)', H1325 same. In context with וב preceding it, this likely represents 'day one' or 'first day' — the phrase וב בת could be a rendering of 'on the first (day)' with בת used in its relational sense (daughter = belonging to). Chose H1323 because it fits the temporal expression for the first day of the week.

בבקר (first instance, consonants ב-ב-ק-ר): Candidates: H1242 'dawn/morning', H1241 'cattle', H1239 'to inspect', H7119 'cool'. The narrative describes women arriving early at a tomb — 'in the morning' is the natural reading. Chose H1242.
בבקר (second instance): Same consonants repeated — an intensifying doubling: 'in the early morning' or 'at the very break of dawn'. Chose H1242.

בקבר (consonants ב-ק-ב-ר): Candidates: H6912 'to inter', H6913 'a sepulchre'. With preposition ב attached, 'to/at the sepulchre' is the coherent reading since they are arriving at a location. Chose H6913.
textual_notes: The phrase וב בת is unusual. It may represent 'and on day one' (first day of the week), with בת functioning as an ordinal marker. The doubling of בבקר בבקר could be emphatic repetition meaning 'very early in the morning' or could reflect a textual duplication.

verses.literal: And on [the] day one in the morning in the morning they came to the tomb carrying spices and ointments that they had prepared

verses.translation: And they found the stone of the sepulchre rolled away [or: overturned, turned over]

translation_notes: אבן (consonants א-ב-ן): Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 same, H70 'a pair of stones / potter's wheel'. A single stone covering a tomb entrance is the natural image. Chose H68.
הקבר (consonants ה-ק-ב-ר): Candidates: H6912 'to inter', H6913 'a sepulchre'. With the definite article ה, this is a noun — 'the sepulchre'. Chose H6913.

verses.literal: And they found [the] stone of the tomb having been overturned

verses.translation: And they entered and did not find the body of Yeshua, the Anointed One [or: the Messiah]

translation_notes: לא (consonants ל-א): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 same (Aramaic). Standard Hebrew negation in a narrative clause. Chose H3808.

גוף (consonants ג-ו-פ): Candidate: H1479 'to hollow or arch, to close/shut'. The consonants ג-ו-פ in later Hebrew mean 'body' (a physical form, something enclosed). The context requires a noun — what they did not find — and 'body' fits perfectly. Chose H1479, understanding the semantic development from 'to enclose' to 'an enclosed form / body'.
ישוע (consonants י-ש-ו-ע): Candidates: H3442/H3443 'Yeshua'. A proper name. Chose H3442.

משיח (consonants מ-ש-י-ח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed one / Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'utterance', H7880 'a shoot/shrub'. The word follows a proper name as a title — 'the anointed one' is the coherent reading. Chose H4899.
textual_notes: גוף as 'body' reflects post-biblical Hebrew usage. The only Strong's entry (H1479) gives 'to hollow/close/shut' — the noun meaning 'body' is a later semantic development from the same root consonants.

verses.literal: And they entered and not they found [the] body of Yeshua [the] Anointed

verses.translation: And while they were terrified [or: bewildered] in their thoughts about this, behold, two men stood close beside them in white and radiant garments

translation_notes: עוד (consonants ע-ו-ד): Candidates: H5749 'to testify/repeat', H5750 'still/yet/while', H5751 same. With preposition ב, 'while still' — a temporal clause. Chose H5750.
הן (consonants ה-ן): Candidates: H2004 'they (fem. emphatic)', H2005 'lo!/if', H2006 'lo/unless'. The subject of 'were alarmed' — feminine plural pronoun referring to the women. Chose H2004.
זה (consonants ז-ה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Demonstrative pronoun following על — 'about this'. Chose H2088.
הנה (consonants ה-נ-ה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Introduces a sudden new element in the narrative — 'behold' is the natural reading. Chose H2009.

ש ני: The word שני ('two') appears split across ש and ני. H5204 'lamentation' for ני alone makes no sense here. The ש is already a relative particle used in this text, but here שני = 'two' preceding 'men'. The split is likely a scribal or tokenization artifact.
להם (consonants ל-ה-ם): Candidates: H3859 'to burn/rankle', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. With preposition ל, this is 'to them' — a prepositional phrase indicating proximity. Chose H1992 as the pronoun.
textual_notes: The word שני ('two') is split across two tokens ש and ני. If ש is the relative particle and ני is standalone, H5204 'lamentation' does not fit. More likely שני is a single word meaning 'two' that was split in tokenization.
לבנים could theoretically parse as ל + בנים (H1143 'space between armies') but the context of garment description makes לבנים = 'white (masc. pl.)' far more natural.

verses.literal: And while that they were alarmed in their thoughts about this behold two men stood near to them in garments white and shining

verses.translation: And the women, when they were afraid, bowed down their faces to the ground, and they [the men] said to them, Why do you seek the living among the dead?

translation_notes: כאשר (consonants כ-א-ש-ר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With כ prefixed to אשר, this is a temporal conjunction — 'when/as'. Chose H834.
והם (consonants ו-ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Third person pronoun introducing a new subject (the two men). Chose H1992.
להם (consonants ל-ה-ם): Same as before — prepositional pronoun 'to them'. Chose H1992.
למה (consonants ל-מ-ה): Candidate: H4100 'what/why/how'. With ל prefix — 'for what reason' = 'why'. Chose H4100.
עם (consonants ע-ם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with/among'. Preposition connecting 'the living' and 'the dead' — 'among/with'. Chose H5973.
textual_notes: תשאלו could derive from שאל 'to ask/inquire' or 'to seek/request'. Both senses work here — 'why do you ask for / seek the living among the dead?'

verses.literal: And the women when they feared and they bowed their faces earthward and they said to them why do you seek the living with the dead

verses.translation: He is not here, for he has returned alive. Remember in what way [or: manner] he spoke with you while he was in the Galilee — and on the Sabbath... [the first of the Sabbath... the first of the Sabbath...]

translation_notes: פה (consonants פ-ה): Candidates: H6310 'mouth', H6311 'here/this place'. The phrase 'he is not ___' requires a locative — 'here'. Chose H6311.
כי (consonants כ-י): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Causal conjunction explaining why he is not here. Chose H3588.
חי (consonants ח-י): Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 same (Aramaic). Predicate describing his state after returning — 'alive'. Chose H2416.

באי (consonants ב-א-י): Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. With preposition ב and followed by זה אופן ('this manner'), this reads 'in what manner' — an interrogative construction. Chose H335.
זה (consonants ז-ה): H2088 'this'. Demonstrative modifying אופן. Chose H2088.

אופן (consonants א-ו-פ-ן): H212 'a wheel'. In later Hebrew, אופן develops the meaning 'manner/way' (as in the turning/mode of something). The context demands 'manner/way' — 'in what manner he spoke'. Chose H212 with the extended semantic sense.
דבר (consonants ד-ב-ר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. A verb is needed — 'he spoke with you'. Chose H1696.
שהיה (consonants ש-ה-י-ה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Relative particle ש + verb היה 'he was' — temporal clause 'that he was [in the Galilee]'. Chose H1961.
בגלילה (consonants ב-ג-ל-י-ל-ה): H1552 'a circuit/region'. With ב prefix and ה suffix — 'in the Galilee (the circuit/region)'. Chose H1552.

ובשבת, שבת, בשבת, שבתאחד, שבת, שבתאחד, שבת: All instances of שבת — Candidates: H7673 'to cease', H7674 'rest/cessation', H7675 'seat/abode', H7676 'Sabbath'. The repeated שבת with אחד appended suggests 'Sabbath-one' = 'the first of the Sabbath/week'. Chose H7676 throughout.
textual_notes: The end of this section (ובשבת שבת בשבת שבתאחד שבת שבתאחד שבת) appears heavily corrupted or contains scribal repetitions. The phrase שבתאחד likely means 'first of the Sabbath/week' but the multiple repetitions are difficult to parse coherently. This may represent a damaged or multiply-copied passage where the scribe repeated phrases. The core meaning appears to be a temporal reference to 'the first day after the Sabbath.'
אופן as 'manner/way' reflects post-biblical Hebrew semantic development from H212 'wheel'.

verses.literal: He is not here for he returned alive remember in what manner he spoke with you while he was in the Galilee and on Sabbath Sabbath on Sabbath Sabbath-one Sabbath Sabbath-one Sabbath

verses.translation: He said that it is necessary [or: required] that the Son of Man be handed over into the hands of sinners, and be hung [or: suspended], and that he will return alive on the third day

translation_notes: אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same (Aramaic), H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. A verb is needed to introduce reported speech. Chose H559.
שבן (consonants ש-ב-ן): ש is the relative particle + בן. Candidates for בן: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 same. 'Son of the man/humanity' is a well-known Semitic title. Chose H1121.

האדם (consonants ה-א-ד-ם): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'a human being/mankind', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. With definite article ה, 'the man / the human' — part of the title 'son of the man'. Chose H120.
חי (consonants ח-י): H2416 'alive'. Describes the state of returning. Chose H2416.
ביום (consonants ב-י-ו-ם): Candidates: H3117 'a day', H3118 same (Aramaic). With preposition ב — 'on the day'. Chose H3117.
textual_notes: ה<לישי appears to have a damaged or missing letter (represented by <). The consonantal skeleton suggests השלישי 'the third', with a shin likely missing.
תלוי could mean 'hung' or 'suspended' — in context this refers to execution by hanging/crucifixion.

verses.literal: [He] said that it is required that [the] son of the man will be delivered into [the] hands of sinners and his being hung and that he will return alive on the day the third

verses.translation: And they remembered his words [or: his sayings]
verses.literal: And they remembered his words

verses.translation: And [they] returned from the sepulchre and reported all these things [or: words, matters] to those eleven and to all the rest

translation_notes: מן (consonants מ-ן): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 same, H4482 'musical chord'. Preposition of origin — 'from the tomb'. Chose H4480.
הקבר (consonants ה-ק-ב-ר): H6912 'to inter', H6913 'sepulchre'. With definite article — a noun. Chose H6913.
כל (consonants כ-ל): H3605 'all/whole', H3606 same. Chose H3605.

אלה (consonants א-ל-ה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. None of these fit. The consonants א-ל-ה also function as the common demonstrative pronoun 'these' (not listed in Strong's as a separate entry but a standard Hebrew word). Context demands a demonstrative — 'all these words'. Chose as demonstrative pronoun 'these'.
אחד עשר: H259 'one' + H6240 'teen/ten in combination' = 'eleven'. A compound number. Chose H259 and H6240.
ולכל: ו + ל + כל H3605 'all'. Chose H3605.
textual_notes: אלה as 'these' (demonstrative pronoun) is not represented in the Strong's candidates provided, which list only nouns/verbs. However, אלה as a demonstrative pronoun is standard Hebrew and is the only coherent reading in this context.

verses.literal: And returning from the tomb and telling all these words to those eleven and to all the others

verses.translation: And it was Miriam of Magdala [or: the Magdalene], and Miriam the mother of Yaakov, and Miriam Shlomit [or: Salome], and the other [women] who were with them, who were telling the sent ones [or: apostles] these things [or: words]

translation_notes: והיה (consonants ו-ה-י-ה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Narrative copula introducing a list — 'and it was'. Chose H1961.
שמרים: ש (relative particle) + מרים H4813 'Miriam'. 'That Miriam...' introducing the named subject. Chose H4813.
אם (consonants א-ם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Followed by a personal name (Yaakov) — 'mother of Yaakov'. Chose H517.
יעקב: H3290 'Yaakov/Jacob'. Proper name. Chose H3290.
אלה (consonants א-ל-ה): Same as section 9 — demonstrative pronoun 'these'. Context: 'these words/things'.
textual_notes: ל<לוחים appears to have a missing letter (marked with <). The consonantal skeleton suggests לשלוחים 'to the sent ones / emissaries / apostles', from the root שלח 'to send'.

The text names three women all called מרים (Miriam). The third מרים is followed by שלומית — this could be a separate name (Shlomit/Salome) or an epithet. It is unclear whether שלומית is a surname or identifies a distinct person.
The third ומרים שלומית could alternatively be parsed as 'and Miriam [called] Shlomit' or 'and Miriam, and Shlomit' with an implied conjunction.

verses.literal: And it was Miriam [the] Magdalite and Miriam mother of Yaakov and Miriam Shlomit and the others that were with them that [were] saying to the sent-ones these words

verses.translation: And these words appeared to them as words not credible [or: not agreed upon] to them, and they did not believe them

translation_notes: להם (both occurrences): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 because the prepositional ל + הם = 'to them' fits the context of reporting words to people.
אלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!', H432 'if'. In later Hebrew אלו functions as a demonstrative pronoun 'these'. Context requires a demonstrative modifying דברים, so reading as 'these'.
ולא: Candidates: H3808, H3809 (both 'not'). Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.
textual_notes: מוסכמין is not a biblical Hebrew form but appears to be a later Hebrew (Mishnaic/Medieval) passive participle from the root ס.כ.מ meaning 'agreed upon, credible'. No Strong's number applies.
האמינום appears to be hifil perfect 3mp of א.מ.נ with 3mp object suffix — 'they believed them'. This is a post-biblical morphological form.

verses.literal: And appeared to them [these] words these as words not agreed-upon to them and not they-believed-them

verses.translation: And Kepha rose and ran to the front of the tomb, and bowing down he saw the burial cloths alone [by themselves], and he went away, amazed [or: wonder-struck] within himself at what had been done

translation_notes: הקבר: Candidates: H6912 'to inter', H6913 'a sepulchre'. Chose H6913 because the article ה + noun 'the tomb' fits — one runs to a tomb, not to a verb.
ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'experiencing', H7203 'seer', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 because the context describes someone looking and seeing cloth — a verb of sight.

לבד: Candidates: H905 'separation/alone', H906 'linen garment', H907 'a lie'. Chose H905 'alone/by themselves' because the point is that only the cloths remained, with no body present. H906 'linen' is tempting alongside 'garments' but would be redundant; the narrative emphasis is on the absence of the body.
והלך: Candidates: H1980 'to walk', H1981 'to walk', H1982 'a wayfarer', H1983 'a journey'. Chose H1980 as the standard verb 'he walked/went away'.
ורץ: H7518 is listed as 'a fragment' but the consonants רץ also correspond to the verb רוץ 'to run'. Context clearly requires 'ran' — he rose and ran to the tomb.
ממה: H4100/H4101 both mean 'what?' — with מ prefix = 'from what'. Chose H4100.
textual_notes: לבד could be read as H906 'linen' (he saw the linen garments) or H905 'alone/by themselves' (he saw the garments alone). Both produce coherent images. I chose 'alone' because the narrative tension concerns the body's absence, making 'the garments by themselves' the more significant observation.
<נעשה has an angle bracket indicating possible textual damage or scribal note. The word appears to be נעשה — nifal of עשה 'was done/made'.
וכורע appears to be a participle of כרע 'to bow/kneel down' — he stooped down to look into the tomb. Not in the Strong's candidates provided but the root is well attested (H3766).

verses.literal: And Kepha rose and ran to before the tomb and bowing-down he-saw the garments alone and he-went to-himself amazed in-himself from-what was-done

verses.translation: And behold, two of them were walking toward a village [or: tower-town] that was far from Jerusalem — forty miles — which is called Emmaus

translation_notes: והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'and behold' naturally introduces a new scene.
מהם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — מ + הם = 'from them/of them'.

במגדול: Candidates: H4024 'Migdol, a place in Egypt', H1419 'great'. The consonants מגדול match מגדל 'tower' (H4026) as well. In context, this is a place name for a town — but the sentence says this place 'is called Emmaus,' so במגדול likely means 'in a town/village' (מגדול as a generic term for a fortified settlement). Chose H4024 as the closest Strong's match for the consonants, but understanding it as a common noun 'tower-town/village' rather than the Egyptian place.
שהיה: Candidates: H1961 'to be/exist', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 — ש + היה = relative 'that' + 'was'.
textual_notes: במגדול is puzzling. The known Emmaus road tradition places it much closer to Jerusalem (about 60 stadia ≈ 7 miles). The text says 'forty miles' which is unusual. מגדול could be a common noun 'tower/fortified place' or a proper name. Since the text immediately clarifies the name as Emmaus, I read במגדול as a generic descriptor 'in a tower-town.'
מילין is an Aramaic/late Hebrew plural of מיל 'mile' (a Roman mile). No Strong's number applies.
שנקרא = ש + נקרא, nifal of קרא 'to call' — 'that is called'. Standard later Hebrew construction.
אימאוס is a transliteration of the place name Emmaus. No Strong's number.

verses.literal: And behold two from-them walking in-a-tower that-was far from-Jerusalem forty miles that-is-called Emmaus

verses.translation: And they were speaking among themselves about that which had been done and [which] had happened [or: occurred] in those days

translation_notes: והם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'and they' as the subject of the participial clause.

מאשר: Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 — מ + אשר = 'from/about that which', a standard relative construction.

וקרה: Candidates: H7135 'coolness', H7136 'to light upon/happen/occur', H7137 'an occurrence'. Chose H7136 because 'happened/occurred' pairs naturally with 'was done' — describing events that took place.
textual_notes: באותן is a later Hebrew demonstrative form 'in those' (ב + אותן). No Strong's number applies directly.
נעשה is nifal of עשה 'to do/make' = 'was done/was made'. No Strong's candidates were provided.

verses.literal: And they speaking between-them from-that [which] was-done and-happened in-those the-days

verses.translation: And while they were speaking among themselves and finding [or: seeking] witnesses, Yeshua drew near to them and [was] walking with them

translation_notes: ובעוד: Candidates: H5749 'to testify/repeat', H5750 'still/yet/while', H5751 same as H5750. Chose H5750 — ב + עוד = 'while still', a temporal conjunction meaning 'while they were still...'.

קרב: Candidates: H7126 'to approach/draw near', H7127 same, H7128 'hostile encounter', H7129 same, H7130 'the center/midst', H7131 'near'. Chose H7126 because the verb 'drew near' fits: Yeshua approached them.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — ל + הם = 'to them'.
ישוע: Candidates: H3442, H3443 (both 'Jeshua'). Chose H3442 as the primary entry for this proper name.
textual_notes: The phrase 'ו מצאו עדים' is difficult. The ו stands alone as a separate word, which is unusual. מצאו could be 'they found' or 'finding'. עדים could be 'witnesses' (from עד H5707) or possibly a form related to עוד. The sequence 'and finding witnesses' before Yeshua's arrival is contextually awkward. This may be a scribal corruption or a phrase meaning something like 'and [while] seeking evidence/testimony,' i.e., they were discussing and trying to make sense of witness accounts when Yeshua appeared.
This entire phrase 'ו מצאו עדים' may be corrupt or may reflect an unusual Hebrew rendering of a source text. The separation of ו from the following word is suspicious.

verses.literal: And while that-they-were speaking between-them and finding witnesses Yeshua drew-near to-them and-walking with-them

verses.translation: And their eyes were blinded [or: sealed shut] so that they were not recognizing him

translation_notes: שלא: ש + לא. Candidates for לא: H3808, H3809 (both 'not'). Chose H3808 — standard negation. ש functions as the relative/conjunction 'that/so that'.
textual_notes: עורות could derive from עור 'to blind/be blind' (H5786/H5787) or from עור 'skin/hide' (H5785) in feminine plural. Context strongly favors 'blinded' — their eyes were blinded so they could not recognize him.
מכירים is a hifil participle of נכר 'to recognize' (H5234). A standard later Hebrew participial construction with היו for ongoing past action.

verses.literal: And-their-eyes blinded so-that-not they-were recognizing him

verses.translation: And Yeshua said: What [are] these words [that] you [are] speaking among yourselves, and already you [are] walking and grieving [or: worrying]?

translation_notes: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — 'said', the standard verb of speech.
באי: Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 — ב + אי = 'in what/which', forming an interrogative with זה: 'in what kind of...'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — the demonstrative. Together באי זה = 'in what kind of / which', a standard later Hebrew interrogative phrase.

וכבר: Candidates: H3527 'to augment', H3528 'long ago/already/hitherto', H3529 'Kebar river', and various entries for בר. Chose H3528 — 'already', fitting the adverbial sense: 'and already you are walking and worrying.'
אתם (both): The only Strong's candidate is H864 'Etham, a place.' But אתם is the standard 2mp pronoun 'you' in Hebrew. No Strong's number for the pronoun was provided; reading as 'you (plural)'.
textual_notes: ודואגים derives from דאג 'to be anxious, worry, grieve' (H1672). This is a participial form = 'and worrying/grieving'. Not listed in candidates but the root is clear.
The phrase באי זה is a compound interrogative 'in what/which' — a standard medieval Hebrew construction.

verses.literal: And-Yeshua said in-which this words you speaking between-you and-already you walking and-worrying

verses.translation: And one of them answered — his name [was] Cleopas — and said to him: You are the one who has recently sojourned [or: been a stranger] in Jerusalem, and you do not know what things have been done in these days?

translation_notes: וענה: Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 same as H6030, H6033 same as H6031, H6034 'Anah'. Chose H6030 — 'answered', the standard response verb in dialogue.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'one of them'.
מהם: H1992 'them' with מ = 'from them'.
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you'. Chose H859 — 'you', the subject of the clause.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/self', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 same. Chose H1931 — 'he/the one', forming with אתה: 'you are the one who...'
גר: Candidates: H1615 'lime', H1616 'a guest/foreigner/sojourner'. Chose H1616 — 'a sojourner/stranger', someone recently dwelling in Jerusalem who apparently doesn't know what happened.
ואמר: H559 'to say'.
אי: Candidates: H335 'where?/what?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 — interrogative 'what/which', forming with זה the compound 'what kind of'.
זה: H2088 'this/that'. Together אי זה = 'which/what'.
באלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!', H432 'if'. In later Hebrew אלו functions as a demonstrative 'these'. With ב = 'in these'. Chose H431 as the closest consonantal match, reading as demonstrative.
textual_notes: ש<מו has an angle bracket suggesting textual damage. The reading is clearly שמו 'his name' (from שם H8034 + 3ms suffix).

ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. The syntax 'and ___ to them' requires a verb of speech; H559 'said' is the clear choice.
שלום (consonants שלום): Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/wholeness', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. As a greeting followed by 'to you', H7965 'peace' is the standard greeting formula.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. As a pronoun before הוא ('he'), 'I' (H589) is the obvious reading.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/it (pronoun)', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. In 'I am he', the demonstrative pronoun H1931 fits naturally.

אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (negative particle, deprecative)', H410 'strength/God', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Before the imperfect תיראו ('you will fear'), H408 as prohibitive 'do not' is the standard Hebrew construction.
להם: This is the preposition ל + 3mp suffix הם. The candidate H3859 'to rankle' does not fit; this is simply 'to them' using the pronoun H1992.

verses.literal: And while they [were] speaking Yeshua stood in their midst and said to them peace to you I [am] he do not fear

verses.translation: And they [were] terrified and trembling — they thought and supposed that they were seeing a spirit [or: wind, breath]

translation_notes: והם (consonants הם): H1992 'they' — pronoun subject, same reasoning as previous sections.

רוח (consonants רוח): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely/revive', H7305 'room/interval', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 'wind/spirit (Aramaic)'. People who are terrified and trembling think they are seeing a ___; 'spirit' (H7307) is the coherent reading — they feared they were seeing a ghost/apparition.
textual_notes: רוח (H7307) has a wide semantic range: wind, breath, spirit, ghost. In context of fearful people thinking they see something supernatural, 'spirit/ghost' is the most fitting sense, but 'breath' (i.e. an apparition or phantom) is also possible.

verses.literal: And they [were] terrified and trembling they thought and supposed that they saw a spirit

verses.translation: And he said to them: Why are you terrified, and what have you thought [or: reasoned] in the midst [or: center] of your hearts?

translation_notes: ואמר (consonants אמר): H559 'to say' — same reasoning as section 6.
להם: Preposition ל + 3mp pronoun הם (H1992) = 'to them'. H3859 'to rankle' does not fit.
למה (consonants מה): Candidates: H4100 'what/how/why', H4101 same (Aramaic). With prefix ל, this forms the interrogative 'why' — H4100.
ומה (consonants מה): H4100 'what' with conjunctive ו — 'and what'.
textual_notes: אתם is listed with only H864 'Etham (a place)' as a candidate, but consonantally אתם is universally the 2mp independent pronoun 'you (masculine plural)'. The Strong's candidate list appears incomplete; this is clearly the pronoun.

verses.literal: And he said to them why [are] you terrified and what did you think in the midst of your hearts

verses.translation: See [or: look at] my hands and my feet

translation_notes: ורגלי (consonants רגלי): Candidate: H7273 'a footman/foot-soldier'. However, consonantally רגלי is naturally 'my feet' (רגל + 1cs suffix). In context of 'see my hands and my ___', 'my feet' is the coherent bodily parallel. H7273 'footman' would break the symmetry of body parts. The suffix -י indicates 'my', pointing to the noun רגל 'foot' with possessive.
textual_notes: ורגלי: The provided candidate H7273 means 'footman/soldier', but the consonants also straightforwardly yield 'my feet' (רגל + 1cs possessive suffix). The parallel with 'my hands' makes 'my feet' virtually certain.

verses.literal: See my hands and my feet

verses.translation: And still they did not believe, marveling from [the] abundance of great joy, and he said: Do you have any thing [or: something] to eat?

translation_notes: שמחה (consonants שמחה): Candidates: H8057 'joy/gladness', H4229 'to wipe/erase'. In 'from abundance of ___ great', 'joy' (H8057) produces the coherent image of people overwhelmed by happiness; 'wiping/erasing' makes no sense.
ואמר (consonants אמר): H559 'to say' — same verb of speech as previous sections.

זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that (demonstrative)', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. In 'any ___ thing to eat', the demonstrative 'this' (H2088) functions as part of the indefinite construction 'some/any kind of thing'.
דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. In 'any ___ to eat', the noun 'thing' (H1697) is the natural reading.
textual_notes: The consonants א י זה appear to be separated in the manuscript. Together they likely form איזה 'which/any kind of', a later Hebrew interrogative/indefinite pronoun. The separation may be a scribal convention or spacing artifact.

verses.literal: And still they [were] not believing and marveling from abundance of joy great and he said is there to you any thing to eat

verses.translation: And they gave him a piece of roasted [or: broiled] fish and one honeycomb of honey

translation_notes: והם (הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham, a region', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Chose H1992 because this is a subject pronoun introducing who performed the action of giving — 'they gave him.'

חלק: Candidates: H2505 'to apportion', H2506 'allotment/portion', H2507 'Chelek (name)', H2508 'a part', H2509 'smooth', H2510 'Chalak (place)'. Chose H2506 because it functions as a noun meaning 'a portion/piece' of fish, which is the natural construct here.
textual_notes: ויערת appears to be a construct form of יער (honeycomb/forest), likely יערת דבש meaning 'honeycomb of honey.' The word is not listed among the candidates but the consonants support this reading from H3293/H3295.
אפוי is a passive participle from אפה (to bake/roast), not listed in candidates but consonantally clear.

verses.literal: And they gave to-him a portion [of] fish roasted and a honeycomb [of] honey one

verses.translation: And when he ate before them [in their presence], he took what remained [the leftover] and gave it to them

translation_notes: אשר (in וכאשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when/because', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר is a temporal conjunction meaning 'when/as,' fitting the narrative sequence.
אכל: Candidates: H398 'to eat', H399 'to eat', H400 'food', H401 'Ucal (name)'. Chose H398 because a verb is needed here — 'when he ate.'
לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction'. Chose H3947 because the context describes a physical action: taking the remaining food.

להם: Candidates under להם: H3859 'to rankle'; under הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 as prepositional ל + הם = 'to them,' which fits giving the remainder to those present.
textual_notes: הנותר is a nifal participle from יתר (to remain/be left over), consonantally clear though not listed in candidates.
ונתנו could be parsed as 'and he gave it' (3ms + 3ms suffix) or 'and they gave' (3mp). Context favors 'and he gave it' since the subject has been singular (he ate, he took).

verses.literal: And when he-ate before-them he-took the-remaining and-gave-it to-them

verses.translation: And he said to them: These are the words that I spoke to you while I was still with you — that it was necessary [obligated] that all the things written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets and in the Psalms concerning me should be fulfilled

translation_notes: אמר (in ואמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because a verb of speaking is required by the narrative context.
להם: Candidates under להם: H3859 'to rankle'; under הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 as ל + הם = 'to them.'

אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. None of these match the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428). The consonants אלה clearly function as the demonstrative pronoun 'these' in context, pointing to the words that follow.
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — functioning as a copula: 'these are they, the words.'
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 'he/it', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — impersonal 'it' in the clause 'that it was obligated.'

שכל: Candidates under שכל: H7919 'to be circumspect', H7920 'intelligent', H7921 'to miscarry', H7922 'intelligence'; under כל: H3605 'the whole/all', H3606 'all'. Chose H3605: ש + כל = 'that all,' introducing the content clause about what must be fulfilled.
בדת: Candidates: H1881 'a royal edict/statute', H1882 same. Chose H1881 — 'law/statute,' here referring to the Torah of Moses.
משה: Candidates: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moses', H4873 'Moses', H4874 'a debt'; under שה: H7716 'sheep/goat'. Chose H4872 because 'the law of Moses' is the natural referent.

עלי: Candidates: H5940 'pestle', H5941 'Eli', H5942 'high', H5943 'supreme'. None match the preposition על + 1cs suffix 'about me/concerning me' (H5921 + suffix). Context demands 'that were said about me.'
textual_notes: אלה as a demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428) is not among the listed candidates, but the consonants are identical and context absolutely demands this reading over 'bewail,' 'imprecation,' 'oak,' or 'God.'
עלי as על + suffix 'concerning me' is the natural reading but was not among the listed Strong's candidates. The alternatives (pestle, Eli, high, supreme) produce no coherent reading here.
שחוייב appears to be a later Hebrew/Aramaic passive form meaning 'it was obligated/necessary' — not a classical biblical Hebrew form, suggesting this text has post-biblical linguistic features.
נשלמים is a nifal participle from שלם meaning 'being completed/fulfilled.'

verses.literal: And-he-said to-them these [are] they the-words that-I-said to-you in-my-standing with-you that-it-is-obligated he that-all the-words will-be fulfilled the-written in-the-law-of Moses and-in-the-prophets and-in-the-psalms that-were-said about-me

verses.translation: Then he opened [unlocked] their understanding [intellect] to know [perceive] the Scriptures [writings] and to understand them

translation_notes: פתח: Candidates: H6605 'to open wide', H6606 'to open', H6607 'door/entrance', H6608 'disclosure'. Chose H6605 because a verb is needed — 'he opened' their understanding.
להם: As before, ל + הם = 'to them' (H1992).

שכלם: The listed candidate כלם H3637 'to wound/insult' does not fit. The consonants שכל match H7922 'intelligence/understanding' with a 3mp suffix ם = 'their understanding.' This produces the coherent image of opening their intellect, whereas 'their wounding/insult' is incoherent.
לדעת: H1847 'knowledge' — with ל prefix this is 'to know/for knowledge.'
textual_notes: שכלם: The only listed candidate (כלם H3637 'to wound') does not fit. Reading as שכל + ם suffix (H7922 'their intelligence/understanding') is strongly supported by context — he opened their understanding to know the writings.
הכתיבות is a feminine plural noun from כתב (to write), meaning 'the writings/scriptures.' Not listed among candidates but consonantally clear.
ולהבינם is a hifil infinitive of בין with ל prefix and 3mp suffix: 'and to cause them to understand/and to understand them.'

verses.literal: Then he-opened to-them their-understanding to-know the-writings and-to-understand-them

verses.translation: And he said to them: Thus it is written, and thus it was necessary [ordained] for Yeshua [the Deliverer] to suffer death and to return alive [rise to life] on the third day

translation_notes: אמר: As before, H559 'to say.'

שכן: Candidates under שכן: H7931 'to reside', H7932 'to reside', H7933 'a residence', H7934 'neighbor'; under כן: H3651 'thus/so', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651: ש + כן = 'that thus/so,' introducing what is written. 'That he should reside written' makes no sense.
וכן: Candidates: H3651 'thus', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — 'and thus/and so.'
לישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua', H3443 same. Chose H3442 — the proper name Yeshua.
המות: Candidates: H4191 'to die', H4192 'title of a song', H4193 'death', H4194 'death'. Chose H4194 — the noun 'death' with the article: 'the death.'
חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 'alive/life'. Chose H2416 — 'alive,' describing the state upon returning.
ביום: Candidates: H3117 'a day', H3118 'a day'. Chose H3117 — 'on the day.'
textual_notes: ה<לישי appears to have a damaged or missing letter (indicated by <). The expected word is השלישי 'the third.' The ש may have been lost in transmission.

כתוב is a passive participle from כתב (H3789 'to write'). The listed candidate תוב H8421 'to reply' does not account for the leading כ unless read as כ + תוב, which would mean 'like replying' — incoherent here. Reading as כתוב 'written' is clearly correct.
חוייב and לסבול are later Hebrew forms not well attested in biblical Hebrew, further suggesting post-biblical provenance of this text.
ולחזור is an infinitive from חזר 'to return,' a post-biblical Hebrew term.

verses.literal: And-he-said to-them that-thus [it is] written and-thus [it was] obligated for-Yeshua to-suffer the-death and-to-return alive on-day the-third

verses.translation: For repentance [returning] and for forgiveness of sins [iniquities] — [this] shall be proclaimed [sought out, preached] to all the peoples [nations], and they shall begin in Jerusalem

translation_notes: לתשובה: H8666 'a recurrence/return/reply.' In context this means 'for returning/repentance' — the turning back that leads to forgiveness.
דרש: H1875 'to tread/seek/inquire/proclaim.' In context, this is the proclamation or preaching to all peoples — the message of repentance and forgiveness shall be sought out/proclaimed.
לכל: H3605 'the whole/all' — 'to all.'
בירושלם: H3390 'Jerusalem.'
textual_notes: דרש could be read as an imperative 'proclaim!', a passive 'shall be proclaimed,' or an infinitive absolute. Context suggests a passive or impersonal sense: repentance and forgiveness shall be proclaimed/preached to all peoples.
ולמחילת is from מחילה 'forgiveness' — a post-biblical Hebrew noun not in the Strong's biblical lexicon, further confirming this text's later Hebrew character.
עונות is plural of עון (H5771 'iniquity/guilt'), not listed among candidates but consonantally unambiguous.
והתחילו is a hitpael or late Hebrew form of חלל/תחל meaning 'and they shall begin,' not classical biblical Hebrew.

verses.literal: For-repentance and-for-forgiveness-of iniquities [it shall be] proclaimed to-all the-peoples and-they-shall-begin in-Jerusalem

verses.translation: And you [yourselves] are witnesses of these things [words, matters]

translation_notes: ואתם: The listed candidate H864 'Etham, a place' is clearly wrong in context. The consonants אתם are the standard 2mp pronoun 'you' (H859). 'And you are witnesses' is the only coherent reading; 'and Etham witnesses' is nonsensical.

מאלה: Candidates: H421 'bewail', H422 'imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. None match. The consonants אלה here function as the demonstrative 'these' (H428), with מ prefix = 'of these.' 'Witnesses of God the words' is possible but less natural than 'witnesses of these things.'
textual_notes: מאלה: Could potentially be read as מ + אלה (H426) = 'from God,' yielding 'witnesses from God of the words.' However, the demonstrative reading 'of these' is far more natural with הדברים following.
עדים: Plural of עד (H5707 'witness'). The ים suffix here is straightforwardly plural — multiple witnesses.

verses.literal: And-you [are] witnesses of-these the-words

verses.translation: And I will send the promise [the vow, the pledged gift] from my Father upon you, and you shall remain [stand firm] in the city until you are clothed [invested] with power from the Most High [the Supreme]

translation_notes: ואני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — 'and I,' the speaker identifying himself as the one who will send.
הנדר: Candidates: H5087 'to promise/vow', H5088 'a promise/vow'. Chose H5088 — the noun 'the promise/vow,' the thing pledged by the Father.
מאבי: The listed candidate H21 'Abi (Hezekiah's mother)' is a proper name that makes no sense here. Reading as מ + אב (H1 'father') + 1cs suffix = 'from my father' is the only coherent option.

בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle'; under עיר: H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young donkey'. Chose H5892 — 'in the city.' Standing in cattle or in a donkey makes no sense. The instruction to remain 'in the city' (Jerusalem, from context) is coherent.
עד: Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'until/as far as', H5705 same, H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux'. Chose H5704 — 'until,' introducing a temporal clause.
עליון: Candidates: H5945 'the Supreme/Most High', H5946 'the Supreme'. Chose H5945 — 'the Most High,' describing the source of power.
textual_notes: בכם: The preposition ב + כם (2mp suffix) could mean 'in you' or 'upon you.' Context of sending a promise suggests 'upon you.'
אשלח is a 1cs imperfect of שלח (H7971 'to send'), not listed among candidates but consonantally unambiguous.
מלובשים is a pual participle of לבש 'to clothe' — 'being clothed/invested.' Post-biblical form.

verses.literal: And-I will-send the-promise from-my-father upon-you and-you will-stand in-the-city until that-you-will-be clothed from-power [of the] Most-High

verses.translation: And he led [conducted] them out to Beit-Aniyah [Bethany] and he lifted up his hands toward the heavens [on high] and blessed them

translation_notes: ונהג: H5090 'to drive forth/lead/carry away.' Chose H5090 — 'and he led them,' a natural narrative action.
בבית: Candidates under בית: H1004 'house', H1005 'house', H1006 'Bajith'; under ית: H3487 'sign of object'. Chose H1004 — 'to the house of' or 'to Bethany' (Beit-Aniyah as a place name).
עניה: H6043 'Anajah/Aniyah.' Combined with בית this gives Beit-Aniyah = Bethany, a known place name.

ונשא: Candidates: H5375 'to lift', H5376 'to lift', H5377 'to lead astray/delude', H5378 'to lend on interest'. Chose H5375 — 'and he lifted' his hands. Lifting hands is a gesture of blessing; leading astray or lending on interest are incoherent here.
textual_notes: ל<מים has a damaged/missing letter (indicated by <). The expected reading is לשמים 'to the heavens/sky.' The ש appears lost in transmission.
וברכם: The consonants allow ו + ברך + ם. Reading as 'and he blessed them' (H1288 + 3mp suffix) fits the gesture of lifting hands.

verses.literal: And-he-led them to-Beit-Aniyah and-he-lifted his-hands to-the-heavens and-blessed-them

verses.translation: And while he was still blessing them, he was separated [parted] from them, and he was carried up [lifted, borne away] into the heavens [the heights]

translation_notes: ובעוד: Candidates: H5749 'to testify/reiterate', H5750 'continuance/still/while', H5751 same. Chose H5750 — 'and while still,' introducing a temporal clause describing ongoing action.
שמברך: Candidates under ברך: H1288 'to bless/kneel', H1289 'to bless', H1290 'a knee', H1291 'a knee'. Chose H1288 — ש + מברך = 'while he was blessing,' a piel participle with prefix ש and מ.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'; under יה: H3050 'Jah'. Chose H1961 — 'he was,' an auxiliary verb: 'he was separated.'
מהם: Under הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — מ + הם = 'from them.'
והוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — 'and he,' the emphatic pronoun identifying who was lifted up.
textual_notes: ב<מים has the same damaged/missing letter as in section 9. The expected reading is בשמים 'in/into the heavens.'
נפרד is a nifal form of פרד (H6504 'to separate/divide') — 'was separated/parted.'
נשוא is a passive participle from נשא (H5375) meaning 'lifted up/carried,' describing the manner of his departure.

verses.literal: And-while he-was-blessing them he-was separated from-them and-he [was] lifted-up into-the-heavens

verses.translation: And they, having worshipped [or: prayed], returned to Jerusalem with great [abundant] joy

translation_notes: והם (consonants ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (region)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. With the prefix ו (and) and followed by a participle מתפללים describing the action of persons, H1992 'they' is the only reading that produces a coherent clause — 'and they praying.'

שמחה (consonants ש-מ-ח-ה): Candidates: H8057 'joy/gladness', or root מחה H4229 'to wipe/erase' with prefix ש. In context of returning to Jerusalem 'in greatness of ___', joy (H8057) produces the natural image; 'in greatness of wiping/erasing' is incoherent.
textual_notes: מתפללים — no Strong's candidates provided; parsed as hitpael participle plural masculine of פלל (to pray/intercede). The hitpael form can mean 'praying' or 'worshipping' (prostrating oneself in prayer).

וחזרו — no Strong's candidates provided; parsed as vav + qal perfect 3rd plural of חזר (to return). This is a common post-biblical Hebrew verb; the biblical equivalent would be שוב. This may indicate a later linguistic stratum of the text.

בגודל — no Strong's candidates provided; parsed as preposition ב + noun גודל (greatness/magnitude). This word is attested in later Hebrew more than biblical Hebrew, again suggesting a post-biblical composition or translation.

verses.literal: And they [were] praying and returned to Jerusalem in greatness [of] joy

verses.translation: And they were in the Temple [sanctuary] at all times, praising and blessing YHWH. Complete [finished].

translation_notes: במקדש (consonants מ-ק-ד-ש): Candidates: H4720 'sanctuary/consecrated place', or roots H6942-H6946 with prefix ב-מ. H4720 as 'in the sanctuary/Temple' fits perfectly — people who returned to Jerusalem praising God would naturally be in the Temple. The other candidates (Kedesh, Kadesh, a sacred prostitute) produce incoherent or bizarre images in this context.
בכל (consonants כ-ל): Candidates: H3605 'the whole/all/every', H3606 (Aramaic equivalent). Both mean the same; H3605 is the Hebrew form. With עת following, 'at every time' = continually.

תם (consonants ת-ם): Candidates: H8535 'complete/pious/gentle', H8536 'there', H8537 'completeness/innocence'. This word appears at the very end of the text. H8537 'completeness' functions as a scribal colophon meaning 'finished/complete' — a standard marker at the end of a scroll or composition. H8535 'pious' could describe YHWH but would be unusual. H8536 'there' (Aramaic) is contextually weak. Chose H8537 as end-marker.
textual_notes: והיו — no Strong's candidates provided; parsed as vav-consecutive/conjunctive + qal imperfect (or simple vav + perfect) 3rd plural of היה (to be). 'And they were' is the natural reading.

משבחים — no Strong's candidates provided; parsed as piel participle plural masculine of שבח (to praise/commend). This root is more common in later Hebrew and Aramaic than in classical biblical Hebrew, reinforcing the impression of a late or post-biblical text.
ומברכים — no Strong's candidates provided; parsed as vav + piel participle plural masculine of ברך (to bless/kneel). Standard Hebrew.

תם at the end: this could be (1) a scribal colophon meaning 'the end / finished', (2) an adjective modifying YHWH ('YHWH [who is] complete/perfect'), or (3) an adverbial sense 'completely.' The colophon reading is most likely given its position as the final word of the entire text.

verses.literal: And they were in the sanctuary at every time praising and blessing YHWH complete
